children.name: Parahucho

children.name: Parahucho perryi
children.description: The Sakhalin taimen, also known as the Japanese huchen or stringfish, is a large species of salmonid freshwater fish in Northeast Asia, found in the lakes and large rivers of Primorsky, Khabarovsk, Sakhalin and Kuril Islands of Far Eastern Russia, as well as Hokkaido of Japan. Although often placed in the genus Hucho, molecular phylogenetic and other evidence has shown that it belongs in its own monotypic genus Parahucho.

children.name: Brachymystax tsinlingensis
children.description: Brachymystax tsinlingensis, also known as the Qinling lenok, is a species of salmonid.

children.name: Brachymystax tumensis

children.name: Hucho

children.name: Hucho bleekeri
children.description: Hucho bleekeri, the Sichuan taimen, is a species of freshwater fish in the salmon family (Salmonidae), endemic to the Yangtze basin in China.

children.name: Hucho taimen
children.description: Siberian taimen, also known as the common taimen, Siberian giant trout or Siberian salmon, is a species of salmon-like ray-finned fish from the genus Hucho in the family Salmonidae. These fish are found in rivers in Siberia and adjacent regions, and are harvested throughout the year.

children.name: Salvelinus

children.name: Salvelinus albus
children.description: Salvelinus albus, also known as white charmander, is a species of freshwater fish in the salmonidae family.

children.name: Salvelinus alpinus
children.description: The Arctic char or Arctic charr is a cold-water fish in the family Salmonidae, native to alpine lakes, as well as Arctic and subarctic coastal waters in the Holarctic. It is the world's most northerly freshwater fish. Some populations are anadromous.

children.name: Salvelinus andriashevi
children.description: Salvelinus andriashevi, also called the Chukot char, is a species of bony fish in the family Salmonidae.

children.name: Salvelinus boganidae
children.description: Salvelinus boganidae is a species of bony fish in the family Salmonidae.

children.name: Salvelinus confluentus
children.description: The bull trout (Salvelinus confluentus) is a char of the family Salmonidae native to northwestern North America.

children.name: Salvelinus curilus
children.description: Salvelinus curilus is a species of anadromous fish in the salmon family.

children.name: Salvelinus drjagini
children.description: Salvelinus drjagini, also known as Dryanin's charr, is a species of freshwater fish in the salmon family.

children.name: Salvelinus elgyticus
children.description: Salvelinus elgyticus is a species of fish in the salmon family, Salmonidae.

children.name: Salvelinus evasus
children.description: Salvelinus evasus, is a vulnerable deepwater char or trout living in the Ammersee lake in Bavaria, Southern Germany.

children.name: Salvelinus fontinalis
children.description: The brook trout (Salvelinus fontinalis) is a species of freshwater fish in the char genus Salvelinus of the salmon family Salmonidae native to Eastern North America in the United States and Canada.

children.name: Salvelinus kronocius
children.description: Salvelinus kronocius, also known in Russian as the "long-headed char" (Длинноголовый голец), is a species of bony fish in the family Salmonidae.

children.name: Salvelinus kuznetzovi
children.description: Salvelinus kuznetzovi, commonly known as stone char, is a species of freshwater fish in the salmon family.

children.name: Salvelinus leucomaenis
children.description: Salvelinus leucomaenis, the whitespotted char, is an East Asian trout in the genus Salvelinus, called iwana in Japanese and kundzha (кунджа) in Russian.

Salvelinus namaycush
children.description: The lake trout is a freshwater char living mainly in lakes in Northern North America. Other names for it include mackinaw, namaycush, lake char (or charr), touladi, togue, laker, and grey trout. In Lake Superior, it can also be variously known as siscowet, paperbelly and lean.

children.name: Salvelinus neiva
children.description: Salvelinus neiva, also known as neiva, is a freshwater species of fish in the salmon family.

children.name: Salvelinus taranetzi
children.description: Salvelinus taranetzi, also known as the Taranets char, is a species of salmonid fish native to Chukotka, Northeast Russia.

children.name: Salvelinus umbla
children.description: Salvelinus umbla, also known as lake char, is a species of char found in certain lakes of the region of the Alps in Europe.

children.name: Salmo
children.description: Salmo — a genus of salmon, trout, char & grayling in the family Salmonidae.

children.name: Salmo abanticus
children.description: The brown trout (Salmo trutta) is a species of carnivorous ray-finned fish and the most widely distributed species of the salmonid genus Salmo, endemic to most of Europe, West Asia and parts of North Africa, and has been widely introduced globally as a game fish, even becoming one of the world's worst invasive species outside of its native range.

children.name: Salmo akairos
children.description: Salmo akairos, known as Moroccan trout or Ifni trout is a species of trout, a salmonid fish, endemic to Lake Ifni, a lake less than one square kilometre in size located at an altitude of in Morocco.

children.name: Salmo aphelios
children.description: Salmo aphelios is a species of trout, a salmonid fish endemic to Lake Ohrid in North Macedonia and Albania in the Balkans.

children.name: Salmo baliki
children.description: Salmo baliki is a species of trout, a type of salmonid fish.

children.name: Salmo carpio
children.description: Salmo carpio, also known as the carpione (carpione del Garda or Lake Garda carpione ), is a salmonid fish endemic to Lake Garda in Italy.

children.name: Salmo caspius

children.name: Salmo cenerinus
children.description: Salmo cenerinus is a species of fish from the family of Salmonidae, in northern Italy from the Po to the Isonzo and on the northern slope of the Apennines.

children.name: Salmo cettii
children.description: Salmo cettii, or the Mediterranean trout, is a species of trout, a freshwater fish in the family Salmonidae.

children.name: Salmo chilo
children.description: Salmo chilo is a salmonid fish, a relative of trout first described as a distinct species in 2012 from the Akdere Stream, a tributary of the Ceyhan River in Turkey.

children.name: Salmo ciscaucasicus
children.description: Salmo ciscaucasicus, the Caspian salmon or Terek trout, is a salmonid fish endemic to the Caspian Sea and its inflowing rivers.

children.name: Salmo coruhensis
children.description: Salmo coruhensis is a species of trout, a freshwater salmonid fish.

children.name: Salmo farioides
children.description: Salmo farioides, commonly known as the West Balkan trout, the Adriatic brown trout, or the Balkan brook trout, is a species of ray-finned fish found in the Balkans, including Albania, Croatia, North Macedonia, among others.

children.name: Salmo fibreni
children.description: Salmo fibreni, or the Fibreno trout, is a freshwater salmonid fish, endemic to Lago di Posta Fibreno in central Italy.

children.name: Salmo ischchan
children.description: The Sevan trout (Salmo ischchan) is an endemic fish species of Lake Sevan in Armenia, known as ishkhan (իշխան, ) in Armenian.

children.name: Salmo kottelati
children.description: Salmo kottelati is a species of trout endemic to the Alakır Stream of Antalya Province in southern Turkey.

children.name: Salmo letnica
children.description: Ohrid trout (Salmo letnica) is an endemic species of trout in Lake Ohrid and in its tributaries and outlet, the Black Drin river, in North Macedonia and Albania.

children.name: Salmo lumi
children.description: Salmo lumi is a type of trout, a fish in the family Salmonidae.

children.name: Salmo macedonicus
children.description: Salmo macedonicus is a species of fish in the family Salmonidae.

children.name: Salmo macrostigma
children.description: Salmo macrostigma, known as Algerian trout, is a species of freshwater trout endemic to Algeria in northwest Africa.

children.name: Salmo marmoratus
children.description: Salmo marmoratus, the marble trout, is a species of freshwater fish in the family Salmonidae.

children.name: Salmo marmoratus x Salmo trutta
children.description: Salmo marmoratus, the marble trout, is a species of freshwater fish in the family Salmonidae.

children.name: Salmo obtusirostris
children.description: Salmo obtusirostris, commonly known as the softmouth trout, also known as the Adriatic trout, or Adriatic salmon, is a species of salmonid fish endemic to a handful rivers spilling into Adriatic in the Western Balkans, in southeastern Europe, namely in Bosnia and Herzegovina, Croatia and Montenegro.

children.name: Salmo ohridanus
children.description: Salmo ohridanus, also known by the local name as the belvica in North Macedonia or belushka in Albania, is a species of freshwater salmonid fish, endemic to Lake Ohrid in Albania and North Macedonia.

children.name: Salmo opimus
children.description: Salmo opimus is a salmonid fish in the genus Salmo.

children.name: Salmo pallaryi
children.description: The Lake Sidi Ali trout (Salmo pallaryi) is an extinct species of salmonid fish that inhabited a single lake in the Atlas Mountains of northern Morocco, at higher than elevation.

children.name: Salmo peristericus
children.description: Salmo peristericus, or the Prespa trout is a variety of trout, a freshwater fish in the family Salmonidae.

children.name: Salmo platycephalus
children.description: Salmo platycephalus, known as the flathead trout, Ala balik or the Turkish trout, is a type of trout, a fish in the family Salmonidae.

children.name: Salmo rhodanensis
children.description: Salmo rhodanensis, or the Rhône trout, is a salmonid fish, a putative species of trout resident in the Rhône river drainage in France and Switzerland.

children.name: Salmo salar
children.description: The Atlantic salmon is a species of ray-finned fish in the family Salmonidae. It is the third largest of the Salmonidae, behind Siberian taimen and Pacific Chinook salmon, growing up to 1 m (3.3 ft) in length. Atlantic salmon are found in the northern Atlantic Ocean and in rivers that flow into it.

children.name: Salmo trutta
children.description: The brown trout (Salmo trutta) is a species of carnivorous ray-finned fish and the most widely distributed species of the salmonid genus Salmo, endemic to most of Europe, West Asia and parts of North Africa, and has been widely introduced globally as a game fish, even becoming one of the world's worst invasive species outside of its native range.

children.name: Oncorhynchus
children.description: Oncorhynchus — a genus of salmon, trout, char & grayling in the family Salmonidae.

children.name: Oncorhynchus clarkii
children.description: The cutthroat trout is a clade of four fish species of the family Salmonidae native to cold-water tributaries of the Pacific Ocean, Rocky Mountains, and Great Basin in North America. These four species are the Coastal, Westslope, Lahontan, and the Rocky Mountain. As a member of the genus Oncorhynchus, it is in the Pacific trout group, which includes the widely distributed rainbow trout.

children.name: Oncorhynchus gilae
children.description: The Gila trout is a species of salmonid, related to the rainbow trout, native to the southwestern United States. Prior to 2006 the Gila trout was federally listed as endangered. In July 2006, after much work by the New Mexico Department of Game and Fish and Arizona Game and Fish Department, the United States Forest Service and the United States Fish and Wildlife Service, the Gila trout was down-listed to threatened, with a special provision called a "4d rule" that will allow limited sport fishing – for the first time in nearly half a century.

children.name: Oncorhynchus gorbuscha
children.description: Pink salmon or humpback salmon is a species of euryhaline ray-finned fish in the family Salmonidae. It is the type species of the genus Oncorhynchus, and is the smallest and most abundant of the seven officially recognized species of salmon. The species' scientific name is based on the Russian common name for this species gorbúša (горбуша), which literally means humpie.

children.name: Oncorhynchus kawamurae
children.description: Black kokanee (Oncorhynchus kawamurae), or in Japanese, is a species of landlocked Pacific trout in Japan that was thought to be extinct for 70 years before being rediscovered in 2010.

children.name: Oncorhynchus keta
children.description: The chum salmon, also known as dog salmon or keta salmon, is a species of anadromous salmonid fish from the genus Oncorhynchus native to the coastal rivers of the North Pacific and the Beringian Arctic. The English name "chum salmon" comes from the Chinook Jargon term tsəm, meaning "spotted" or "marked"; while keta in the scientific name comes from Russian, which in turn comes from the Evenki language of Eastern Siberia.

children.name: Oncorhynchus kisutch
children.description: The coho salmon (Oncorhynchus kisutch) is a species of anadromous fish in the salmon family and one of the six Pacific salmon species.

children.name: Oncorhynchus masou
children.description: The masu salmon (Oncorhynchus masou), also known as masu ( ) or in Japan, is a species of salmonid belonging to the genus Oncorhynchus, found in the North Pacific along Northeast/East Asian coasts from the Russian Far East (Primorsky, Kamchatka Peninsula, Sakhalin and Kuril Islands) to south through Korea, Japan and Taiwan.

children.name: Oncorhynchus mykiss
children.description: The rainbow trout is a species of trout native to cold-water tributaries of the Pacific Ocean in North America and Asia. The steelhead is an anadromous (sea-run) form of the coastal rainbow trout (O. irideus) or Columbia River redband trout (O.

children.name: Oncorhynchus nerka
children.description: The sockeye salmon (Oncorhynchus nerka), also called red salmon, kokanee salmon, blueback salmon, or simply sockeye, is an anadromous species of salmon found in the Northern Pacific Ocean and rivers discharging into it.

children.name: Oncorhynchus tshawytscha
children.description: The Chinook salmon is the largest and most valuable species of Pacific salmon. Its common name is derived from the Chinookan peoples. Other vernacular names for the species include king salmon, quinnat salmon, tsumen, spring salmon, blackmouth, and tyee salmon.

children.name: Thymallus
children.description: Thymallus — a genus of salmon, trout, char & grayling in the family Salmonidae.

children.name: Thymallus arcticus
children.description: The Arctic grayling (Thymallus arcticus) is a species of freshwater fish in the salmon family Salmonidae.

children.name: Thymallus baicalensis
children.description: Thymallus baicalensis, also known as the Baikal black grayling, is a Siberian freshwater fish species in the salmon family Salmonidae.

children.name: Thymallus baicalensis x Thymallus baicalolenensis
children.description: Thymallus baicalensis, also known as the Baikal black grayling, is a Siberian freshwater fish species in the salmon family Salmonidae.

children.name: Thymallus brevipinnis
children.description: Thymallus brevipinnis is a species of freshwater ray-finned fish belonging to the subfamily Thymallinae, the graylings, part of the family Salmonidae.

children.name: Thymallus brevirostris
children.description: The Mongolian grayling (Thymallus brevirostris) is a freshwater species of fish of the genus Thymallus endemic to the landlocked rivers in Mongolia, Inner Mongolia Province of China and nearby parts of Russian far east.

children.name: Thymallus grubii
children.description: The Amur grayling (Thymallus grubii) is a species of freshwater ray-finned fish from the genus Thymallus (graylings) of the family Salmonidae, endemic to the Amur basin in Russian Far East and Northeast China and also the Onon and Kherlen basins in Mongolia.

children.name: Thymallus ligericus
children.description: Thymallus ligericus, the Loire grayling, is a European freshwater fish species in the salmon family Salmonidae.

children.name: Thymallus mertensii
children.description: The Kamchatka grayling (Thymallus mertensii) is a grayling in the salmon family Salmonidae.

children.name: Thymallus nigrescens
children.description: Thymallus nigrescens, also known as the Hovsgol grayling, is a species of freshwater fish in the salmon family.

children.name: Thymallus thymallus
children.description: Thymallus thymallus, harjus, the grayling or European grayling, is a species of freshwater fish in the salmon family Salmonidae.

children.name: Thymallus tugarinae
children.description: Thymallus tugarinae, also known as the Lower Amur grayling, is a species of freshwater fish in the salmon family.

children.name: Thymallus yaluensis
children.description: Thymallus yaluensis, also known as Yalu grayling, is a putative species of freshwater ray-finned fish in the genus Thymallus (graylings) of the family Salmonidae.

children.name: Stenodus
children.description: Stenodus — a genus of salmon, trout, char & grayling in the family Salmonidae.

children.name: Stenodus leucichthys
children.description: Stenodus leucichthys, also known as the inconnu, sheefish, ak balyk, or beloribitsa, is a species of large, anadromous, freshwater whitefish in the family Salmonidae.

children.name: Prosopium
children.description: Prosopium — a genus of salmon, trout, char & grayling in the family Salmonidae.

children.name: Prosopium coulterii
children.description: The pygmy whitefish (Prosopium coulterii) is a freshwater whitefish of the genus Prosopium in the family Salmonidae.

children.name: Prosopium cylindraceum
children.description: The round whitefish (Prosopium cylindraceum) is a freshwater species of fish that is found in North American drainages from Alaska to New England, including the Great Lakes except for Lake Erie, and in Arctic tributaries of northeast Asia, as well as northern Kamchatka Peninsula and the northern coasts of the Sea of Okhotsk.

children.name: Prosopium gemmifer
children.description: The Bonneville cisco (Prosopium gemmifer) is a freshwater cisco endemic to Bear Lake along the Utah-Idaho border of the United States.

children.name: Prosopium spilonotus
children.description: The Bonneville whitefish (Prosopium spilonotus) is a salmonid fish endemic to Bear Lake on the Utah-Idaho border.

children.name: Prosopium williamsoni
children.description: The mountain whitefish (Prosopium williamsoni) is one of the most widely distributed salmonid fish of western North America.

children.name: Coregonus

children.name: Coregonus albellus
children.description: Coregonus albellus, the autumn brienzlig or the Bernese whitefish, is a species of freshwater ray-finned fish belonging to the family Salmonidae, which includes the salmon, trout, whitefish and graylings.

children.name: Coregonus albula
children.description: Coregonus albula, known as the vendace or as the Least cisco, Lithuania, Sweden, Russia and Estonia, and in some lakes of Norway, the United Kingdom, northern Germany, and Poland.

children.name: Coregonus alpinus
children.description: Coregonus alpinus is a species of freshwater whitefish in the family Salmonidae.

children.name: Coregonus anaulorum
children.description: Coregonus anaulorum is a species of freshwater whitefish in the family Salmonidae.

children.name: Coregonus arenicolus
children.description: thumb | right | Four species of coregonus in Switzerland Coregonus arenicolus is a freshwater fish of the family Salmonidae found in Lake Constance (Switzerland, Germany and Austria).

children.name: Coregonus artedi
children.description: Coregonus artedi, commonly known as the cisco, is a North American species of freshwater whitefish in the family Salmonidae.

children.name: Coregonus autumnalis
children.description: The Arctic cisco (Coregonus autumnalis), also known as Arctic omul ( ), is an anadromous species of freshwater whitefish that inhabits the Arctic parts of Siberia especially Yenisey Gulf.

children.name: Coregonus baicalensis
children.description: Coregonus baicalensis is a species of freshwater whitefish in the family Salmonidae.

children.name: Coregonus bavaricus
children.description: Coregonus bavaricus, the Ammersee kilch, is a species of freshwater whitefish endemic to Lake Ammersee in the German state of Upper Bavaria.

children.name: Coregonus candidus
children.description: Coregonus candidus, locally known as shiny whitefish, is a freshwater species of fish of the genus coregonus, which is also known as whitefish, found in the Lake Neuchâtel and Bienne of Switzerland.

children.name: Coregonus clupeaformis
children.description: The lake whitefish is a species of freshwater whitefish from North America. Lake whitefish are found throughout much of Canada and parts of the northern United States, including all of the Great Lakes. The lake whitefish is sometimes referred to as a "humpback" fish due because of its small head size in relation to the length of the body.

children.name: Coregonus confusus
children.description: Coregonus confusus is a freshwater whitefish from Switzerland.

children.name: Coregonus fontanae
children.description: Coregonus fontanae, also known as the Stechlin cisco, Fontane cisco, or Fontane's cisco, is a putative species of freshwater whitefish in the family Salmonidae endemic to the Großer Stechlinsee in northern Germany.

children.name: Coregonus gutturosus
children.description: Coregonus gutturosus, the Lake Constance whitefish, is an extinct species of whitefish in the salmon family Salmonidae.

children.name: Coregonus hoyi
children.description: Coregonus hoyi, also known as the bloater, is a species or form of freshwater whitefish in the family Salmonidae.

children.name: Coregonus huntsmani
children.description: The Atlantic whitefish (Coregonus huntsmani) is a coregonine fish inhabiting some freshwater lakes within Nova Scotia, Canada.

children.name: Coregonus laurettae
children.description: The Bering cisco or Lauretta whitefish (Coregonus laurettae) is a freshwater whitefish found in Alaska and part of Russia.

children.name: Coregonus lavaretus
children.description: Coregonus lavaretus is a species of freshwater whitefish, in the family Salmonidae.

children.name: Coregonus macrophthalmus
children.description: Coregonus macrophthalmus is a freshwater fish of the family Salmonidae.

children.name: Coregonus maraena
children.description: Coregonus maraena, referred to in English as the maraene, maraena whitefish, It is an extremely important fish within the Baltic Sea ecosystem, both for population equilibrium and for the local diets of the surrounding human population.

children.name: Coregonus maraenoides
children.description: The Peipsi whitefish (Coregonus maraenoides) is a freshwater whitefish of the family Salmonidae that naturally occurs in Lake Peipus on the border of Estonia and Russia, from where it also ascends to Lake Võrtsjärv to spawn.

children.name: Coregonus nasus
children.description: 200px|thumb|Frozen broad whitefish The broad whitefish (Coregonus nasus) is a freshwater whitefish species.

children.name: Coregonus nigripinnis
children.description: The blackfin cisco (Coregonus nigripinnis) was a North American salmonid fish in the freshwater whitefish sub-family Coregoninae.

children.name: Coregonus oxyrinchus
children.description: Coregonus lavaretus is a species of freshwater whitefish, in the family Salmonidae.

children.name: Coregonus palaea
children.description: Coregonus palaea is a species of freshwater fish in the salmon family.

children.name: Coregonus sardinella
children.description: Coregonus sardinella, known as the least cisco or the sardine cisco, is a fresh- and brackishwater salmonid fish that inhabits rivers, estuaries and coastal waters of the marginal seas of the Arctic Basin, as well as some large lakes of those areas.

children.name: Coregonus tugun
children.description: Coregonus tugun, the tugun, is a species freshwater whitefish from rivers draining to the Arctic Ocean.

children.name: Coregonus ussuriensis
children.description: The Amur whitefish (Coregonus ussuriensis) is a species of freshwater whitefish.

children.name: Coregonus wartmanni
children.description: Coregonus wartmanni is a freshwater fish of the family Salmonidae found in Lake Constance (Austria, Germany and Switzerland).

children.name: Coregonus widegreni
children.description: Coregonus widegreni, also called the Valaam whitefish, is a putative species of freshwater whitefish, a part of the common whitefish complex (Coregonus lavaretus sensu lato) from Northern Europe.

children.name: Coregonus zenithicus
children.description: The shortjaw cisco (Coregonus zenithicus) is a North-American freshwater whitefish in the salmon family.

children.name: Coregonus zugensis
children.description: Coregonus zugensis, also known as the Swiss whitefish, was a freshwater species of fish of the subfamily Coregoninae which was found in Europe lakes of Lucerne and Zug.
